title: dot11decrypt: Fix TKIP broadcast frame decryption
description:
For WPA2 mixed mode (CCMP+TKIP) the EAPOL key_version can't be used
to determine that TKIP method is used. The cipher suite for the group
key must instead be used. Fix TKIP broadcast frame decryption by
adding a check on used group cipher suite.

Add also a test case to avoid future regression.

Solves: #19994

notes.body: If for nothing else, thank you for adding the #defines for the cipher suites!

> For WPA2 mixed mode (CCMP+TKIP) the EAPOL key_version can't be used to determine that TKIP method is used. The cipher suite for the group key must instead be used.

Should this either quote, or point to a section of, a spec, to point out why the code works the way it does?

Adding a reference might be good, at least adding something in the code. I'll have to read the specs more closely to find a good reference, maybe IEEE 802.11-2020 12.2.4 RSNA establishment where cipher suite selection is mentioned. 

Key version == 1 according to spec means "ARC4 encryption with HMAC-MD5". TKIP is enhanced WEP and WEP uses ARC4 encryption so deducing TKIP from that is probably correct. That's what the original code successfully used in the past. This covers the non-RSNA (WPA1) case. For RSNA (WPA2) case cipher suite selection should be used.

Git bisect lead me to this commit I merged in 2019:
7638ea013d dot11decrypt: Dynamic sized TK, KEK, KCK, PTK

Here a hack to deduce broadcast SA TKIP cipher from the GTK length was replaced with cipher suite selection. This if I remember correctly was needed as with support for different key length the original check would block CCMP256/GCMP256.

That change fixed the SA cipher selection though the decryption step still had the original check for key version only, now missing the cipher suite check needed.
IEEE 802.11 spec references added.
fix align/indent ?
I found no tab size that worked with the existing code but chose to keep tabs. The added code aligns with tab size 4. Perhaps we should convert the dot11decrypt code to whitespace alignment instead?

> The added code aligns with tab size 4.

Tab stops, with "tab" referring to the ASCII HT character, should not be assumed to be at position 1+4*N*, as the UN\*X standard is 1+8*N*.

> Perhaps we should convert the dot11decrypt code to whitespace alignment instead?

Probably, given that tab stops in some editing software might *not* default to 1+8*N*. (Annoyingly, one such program is the editor in a certain UNIX IDE whose name begins with "X" and ends with "code"; when I first ported the Solaris autofs, I forcibly set the tab width to 8, as that's the tab width for Sun's code, and the default tab width of 4 made the code look like a mess.)
Any white-space cleanups should NOT be part of this change. These "dot11" files are ripe for serious revision in this regard.

commits_data.title: dot11decrypt: Fix TKIP broadcast frame decryption
commits_data.message:
dot11decrypt: Fix TKIP broadcast frame decryption

For WPA2 mixed mode (CCMP+TKIP) the EAPOL key_version can't be used
to determine that TKIP method is used. Instead as per IEE 802.11
specifications the encryption method used for pairwise and group
traffic is negotiated through cipher suite selection. Fix TKIP
broadcast frame decryption by adding a check on used group cipher
suite.

Add also a test case to avoid future regression.

Solves: #19994
